title: Design Twitter
summary: Implement a service with postTweet, getNewsFeed, follow, and unfollow.

contractDetails.constraints: User IDs are integers from 1 through 500. Tweet IDs are distinct integers from 0 through 10,000. There are at most 30,000 calls. A user cannot follow themself. The fixture uses [0,user,tweet], [1,user], [2,follower,followee], and [3,follower,followee] for the four methods in the order above. It collects only the feed results.

statement: Implement a service with postTweet, getNewsFeed, follow, and unfollow. A feed contains up to ten tweet IDs from the user and the people they currently follow. Return IDs from newest to oldest by posting order. Repeated follows have no extra effect, and unfollowing someone who is not followed changes nothing.

examples.explanation: Tweet 3 is newest even though its ID is smaller.
Unfollowing hides that author's old tweets too.
A user sees their own tweet after posting.

constraints: User IDs are integers from 1 through 500. Tweet IDs are distinct integers from 0 through 10,000. There are at most 30,000 calls. A user cannot follow themself. The fixture uses [0,user,tweet], [1,user], [2,follower,followee], and [3,follower,followee] for the four methods in the order above. It collects only the feed results.
hints: Conceptual: A person's newest tweet can be checked without scanning all of their older tweets.
Directional: Store each author's history and use posting sequence numbers as priorities.
Implementation: For a feed, merge the latest available tweet from each eligible author using a max heap. After emitting one, offer its author's previous tweet.
complexityAnalysis: Posting, following and unfollowing take O(1) amortized or expected time with arrays and sets. A feed takes O((f+10) log(f+2)) time and O(f+1) extra space for f followees. Stored tweets and follow edges occupy O(T+E) space.
